brands.name: Maurice Cole Surfboards
brands.short_description: Maurice Cole — pioneering Australian performance design.

models.name: Reverse Vee Shorty
models.description: Revisiting a classic bottom curve, for an all around shortboard. Designed for waves 0-6ft. Vee in the nose for easy paddling, easy take-offs and is great in chop. It has that extra squirt of the bottom with a hard edge the full length of the board. A slight Vee in the tail making for speed and carves.

models.name: Protow
models.description: The most advanced surfboard on the market. Designed for waves 2-8ft. The step up board from the Metro-TT. Now a 1/4" vee in the nose deflects chop and decreases wind lift in large conditions. There is also more thickness under the chest, with a flat deck and a chined rail. Concave sits at 3/8" graduating to a 1/2" vee off the tail for more grip and a rail line flip behind the fins which releases at high speeds. Based on the tow series evolution.

models.name: Vee Con III
models.description: The best board you'll ever ride. Designed for waves 0-10ft. An all around high performance board (short or long) that can be made in sizes from 5'8" to 9'6" and comes in a thruster configuration. It uses the Reverse Vee bottom curve with a more pronounced Vee in the nose, through to a concave to the fins and then a small Vee in the tail. Comes with fluted flyers that act as wings and hard edges nose to tail.

models.name: Mermaid
models.description: The all-rounder. Designed for waves 1-4ft. Maurice's mainstay performance design for small waves — a board designed to replace anything fishy. Approximately 1 to 2 inches shorter and 1/4 to 1/2 an inch wider than your standard shortboard. The wider tail helps carry you over flatter sections and the extra curve in the tail keeps it loose and snappy.

models.name: Metro iD
models.description: The Modern Retro — updated. Designed for waves 1-5ft. The Metro combines width and thickness from the old retro fish, but introduces a tow inspired bottom rocker and a very deep concave. More width in the tail creates a larger sweet spot and an accentuated change in curve at the 1 mark loosens the board up. This board replaces all Fish type boards.

models.name: ATM
models.description: The Magic Board. Designed for waves 2-12ft. The closest Maurice makes to a conventional board. It has a deeper concave than most designs with a lot of tail kick, which means a bit faster and carvier than your current ride. Used in grommet boards, shortboards, semi-guns, and bigger Indo/Hawaii guns up to 10 foot. Custom is King.

models.name: Reverse Vee Twin Pin
models.description: A modern take on a magic board. Designed for waves 1-10ft. The new modern day MC twin fin, designed with the history of Maurice riding a board in the 80s given to him by Dane Kealoha. It has vee in the nose, to concave, to a slight vee in the tail, which gives lots of speed. Fluted flyers with hard edges nose to tail, fins moved up to 11". The fluted flyers give a loose feel and shorten the turning radius.

models.name: Red Dingo
models.description: The crowd crusher. Designed for waves 1-5ft. Maurice's answer to the Mini Longboard/Mal — a very high performance board from 6'8"-9'6", single concave hard edges, comes as a 5 fin to be ridden as thruster or quad and outperforms the 2+1 or single.

models.name: Shiva
models.description: A board for every day. Designed for waves 1-8ft. Born from a desire to create a design that would work as a single, a quad, and a thruster so Roark could travel with a one-board quiver. Single concave with a hard edge nose to tail, a spiral vee off the tail, and very low rocker. Comes in sizes from 5'4"-8'0".

models.name: Twuster
models.description: The Modern Twin. Designed for waves 1-6ft. Redesigned so it can be ridden in small surf as a twin, but also as a thruster when the waves are bigger and you need more grip and drive. Single concave with hard edges nose to tail and an accentuated vee off the Swallow/SWAT tail, with an old school winger. Comes in 5'4"-8'0".

models.name: Dirty Dingo
models.description: The ultimate groveller. Designed for waves 1-5ft. A small wave hybrid that comes as a 5 fin and has the MC DNA of a single concave with hard edges nose to tail and low rocker. Works from knee high to overhead. Comes in a rounded squash tail or squound tail; because of the wider nose it can be surfed smaller than your height.

models.name: Asymmetric
models.description: A new frontier. Designed for waves 1-8ft. For surfers that have used the MC Protow or other boards with a single, deep concave. Allows you to surf solid waves on a much shorter board due to thickness and width hidden by the concave. The rail is more drawn out, giving the feeling of a step-up shortboard without the unwanted foam.

models.name: Metro
models.description: The Modern Retro. Designed for waves 1-5ft. Combines width and thickness from the old retro fish, but introduces a tow inspired bottom rocker and a very deep concave. More width in the tail creates a larger sweet spot. Unlike an old school fish, the Metro will sit high on steep fast sections and won't morph into a shopping trolley style slide when you want to lay a full tilt cutback.

models.name: Reverse V
models.description: The board that changed everything. Designed for waves 2ft plus. In 1990 Tom Curren and Maurice Cole began a surfing/shaping relationship that resulted in Tom winning the World Title from trials to World Champion on a quiver ranging from 6'-8'3". The Reverse V put vee under the front foot and nothing between the fins — the opposite of the old theory — and produced a much faster surfboard that carves at higher speeds.

models.name: Tow
models.description: Designed for waves 6-30ft. Maurice Cole's tow-in design: a substantial 3/4" concave running the length of the board for less wetted surface, a very straight/fast centre bottom line, and curve for turning on the rail line. Construction ranges from multilayered fibreglass hulls to carbon/kevlar and high-grade carbon with 80/20 foil fins.

models.name: RCJ Tow
models.description: Ross Clarke-Jones tow board. Designed for waves 6-30ft. Developed with Ross Clarke-Jones as test pilot on boards generally 5'11" x 16 1/4" x 1 3/4, attaining speeds anywhere up to 120km/h. Hull shape, fin placement, angle, stiffness, size, and foil are all tuned for those speeds.

models.name: Guns
models.description: Designed for waves 6-30ft. Developed with Noah Johnson: a gun that paddles in with ease but can be turned 3/4 of the way down the face and into the barrel, avoiding the drawn-out bottom turn. Hard edge nose to tail, vee in the nose, slight concave into a quad fin setup, thickness under the chest with thin rails and a foiled-out tail. Narrow nose so wind does not get under it when paddling in.
